hypothesis: A substantial fraction of unfinished capability families share a small set of reusable bounded decision primitives that can be implemented by Brain-owned Jev-style decision kernels, leaving deterministic software, JIT knowledge, and genuinely generative residuals separate.
why_now: The remaining 17 unfinished families are already grouped into shared residual lanes. Before family-by-family harvesting or training, test whether cross-domain choice and judgment can share one decision substrate.

candidate_probe_substrates.role: open trained decision heads/adapters and datasets for later donor-independent evaluation

experiment.stage_0: Run oracle self-test to verify Brain probe mechanics.
experiment.stage_1: Run the exact same Brain probe against a Simple-JEV-compatible public endpoint across multiple domains.
experiment.stage_2: If stage_1 shows nontrivial cross-domain competence, replace synthetic sanity cases with frozen spent/public calibration tasks and an untouched held-out set. Compare shared versus per-domain heads and generator-only baseline.
experiment.stage_3: Only after causal benefit is established, test the smallest locally runnable permissive checkpoint/configuration and perform ablation, rescue, specificity, held-out, donor-deletion and exact-Brain-route verification.

interpretation.stage_1_pass_means: The common decision interface is technically viable across domains and merits harder falsification.
interpretation.stage_1_pass_does_not_mean: Opus parity, capability ownership, causal sufficiency, or a need to train a new model.
interpretation.stage_1_fail_means: Localize whether the failure is model choice, prompt/interface, primitive definition, or the shared-kernel hypothesis before any training.

stop_rule: If an already-owned deterministic or simpler reusable route meets the target bar, stop neural harvesting for that primitive.
